item.description:
Arma preview. Chromium 158.0.8127.90 and 27 improvements from upstream.
### New - Undo brings back the tabs Clear put away. - The command palette can list Sites before search, and Control-W closes the highlighted recent tab. - Downloads open, share and save on iPhone and iPad. - The sidebar's scroll bar can be dragged and follows Show scroll bars.
### Improved - Keys typed right after opening the palette are kept, and Return acts on what was typed. - Closing a tab with no earlier tab to return to shows the tab beside it; after reading links opened in the background, closing moves on to the next one. - Pages appear as soon as they first paint, and reawakened tabs reload. - Pinned tab icons stay visible and dim without flicker. - A newly opened tab is revealed in the sidebar. - An open PDF prints its own pages.
### Fixed - ⌘W with the search field open closes only the field. - Modified clicks on SVG links and script-opened windows open a new tab. - Pages stay in their window entering and leaving full screen. - A WebKit page's print job no longer quits the app. - An unloaded tab no longer loads another in its place. - The window buttons stay put with a right-side sidebar. - Chromium 158.0.8127.90 with four community engine fixes.

Arma preview. Nine community improvements from upstream.
### New - Return to Saved URL in the Tabs menu, the command palette and Settings › Shortcuts. - An option, off by default, asks before quitting. - An option, off by default, shows a hidden sidebar for a moment after a Space shortcut.
### Improved - Typing "settings" in the command palette finds Settings pages. - The palette's keyboard selection stays put under a resting pointer. - A new folder made from a tab's menu opens its name for typing. - While a Peek is open, the address field, Copy URL and Site Controls follow the Peek's page. - The sidebar texture stays visible with Reduce Transparency.

Arma preview. Middle-click unloads folder tabs again, and agents hear when Arma is busy.
### Fixed - Middle-clicking a tab in a folder, or a preview card, unloads it as it does elsewhere in the sidebar.
### Improved - An agent that can't connect is told whether Arma isn't running, is at its agent limit, or was updated since it connected.

Arma preview. Arma's own name everywhere: every file, message and download is Arma's.
### Improved - Arma names itself Arma in every message, permission prompt, menu and file it saves. - The classic theme is now called Classic. - The app's own files, its engine and its content filter downloads all carry Arma's name, and the content filter is built by Arma.

Arma preview. Tidy, per-site zoom, smoother scrolling and a shared Picture in Picture player across engines.
### New - Tidy groups your open tabs by topic. - Page zoom is remembered per site in each browsing profile.
### Improved - Picture in Picture uses one player across Chromium and WebKit, with smoother resizing. - The sidebar holds 120 fps across large tab lists, and Settings and window transitions scroll and animate more smoothly. - Arma's engine and content filter downloads are published under Arma's name.

Arma preview. Upstream's smoother sidebar scrolling with many tabs.
### Improved - The sidebar scrolls smoothly even with hundreds of tabs open.

Arma preview. Built on upstream's rebuilt passwords and autofill, with Arma's password features carried over, and Chromium 158.0.8127.89.
### New - Upstream's rebuilt passwords and autofill, with Settings › Autofill and new save and fill prompts. - The Save password? prompt closes on its own after a time you choose, or from its corner. - Pause Arma's password prompts on a tab, from the save prompt or with @passwords. - Choose how long a generated password is and which characters it uses. - Choose how often showing a saved password asks you to authenticate. - A Space can let private windows suggest its saved passwords on secure sites. Private windows still save nothing. - A saved password can fill its websites' subdomains: turn on Include Subdomains when editing it. - Type @passwords in the command palette to copy, fill or open a saved login. - `arma passwords` reaches a Space's saved passwords from the terminal once you unlock it with Touch ID.
### Fixed - A saved password now fills on every website added to it, not only the one it was saved for. - Two-step sign-ins that move between a site's subdomains now save correctly.
### Improved - Chromium 158.0.8127.89.

Arma preview. Settings keeps its light or dark look while a color popover is open.
### Fixed - Opening a color popover in Settings, such as a crest part's, no longer switches the Settings page between light and dark while it is open.
### Internal - The screen eyedropper keeps its sampler alive for the button's lifetime instead of making one per click.

Arma preview. Opens the 0.11 line with upstream 0.11.0 (#1331 to #1343) and Chromium 158, keeps the crest and the theme apart on a Space's page, and lets a theme keep crests by name.
### New - A theme can keep crests by name. On a Space's Appearance page the Theme heading of its icons shows the crests its theme keeps, Add Current Crest saves the Space's crest there with its colors, and a kept crest's menu renames or removes it. Theme files carry them. - arma theme crests, arma theme crest add, rename and remove, and arma crest use manage and wear the crests a theme keeps from the terminal. - Every color popover, for a crest's parts and a theme's colors alike, has an eyedropper that picks a color from anywhere on screen and applies it at once. - From upstream: Site Controls replace the site menus on Mac, iPhone and iPad; a Space's icon is chosen apart from its colors; color popovers take a hex code and offer the system picker; menu items carry icons.
### Improved - A Space's Appearance page now shapes only its crest. The Theme row heads the page as its first setting, the stage shows a color for each part of the crest, and More Customization holds the crest's parts alone, stepping aside for a symbol or emoji icon. Modify Theme Too is gone: themes change only under Settings › Themes. - Under Settings › Themes the presets start folded, so a stray click no longer replaces a theme's colors, and Restore Original sits beside the theme's name. A theme's folder tint has one strength control, Folder colors. - Catppuccin Macchiato's folders wear a lighter lavender back with a black outline, colored at a quarter strength. - Chromium 158 opens every Space with its tabs again, and Arma's automation follows Chromium 158's DevTools.
### Internal - Arma's Chromium engine is Chromium 158.0.8127.37, universal.

Arma preview. Synced with upstream 8ecda9450 (#1302 to #1318), runs on macOS 15 and later, ships as one universal download for Apple silicon and Intel, and returns closed pinned and saved tabs to their saved address.
### New - Arma for Mac now runs on macOS 15 Sequoia and later. On macOS 15, controls that stand on Liquid Glass on macOS 26 stand on Arma's own material instead, and pages translate when you choose Translate rather than automatically.
### New - A Space's Appearance page has Modify Theme Too, off to begin with. On, edits there save over a theme named for the Space, and choosing a house crest starts the whole look over from the house's own. - Settings › Themes can restore a theme to how it was when it was installed or imported, taking back every change made to it since. Undo takes that back too.
### Fixed - Choosing a house crest in a Space's Crest Studio changes only the crest. The Space keeps its theme's colors.
### Improved - Closing a pinned or saved tab returns it to its saved address, unless you choose Resume Last Location in Settings › Tabs. - In the command palette, typing the start of an open or pinned tab's name or site, or of a site you use, puts it first again, so Return goes there instead of searching. Phrases still search first. - Pages opening in dark mode go straight from the loading screen to the page, without a flash of white in between. - In dark mode, the space behind pages, Getting Started, the command palette and the other screens is black, as in Settings, instead of navy. - Panels, notices, drag previews, Peeks and setup's windows now cast one consistent set of shadows, so surfaces at the same height look the same everywhere. - Disabled glyph buttons, such as reload, fade to the same strength as every other disabled glyph. - On Mac, a shortcut button you're recording a shortcut into is tinted blue instead of the system accent color. - Text buttons and setup's welcome line on iPhone and iPad grow with your text size, and setup's welcome on iPad scrolls at the largest sizes so Continue stays in reach.
### Internal - The Mac app, its native core, its helpers and the Chromium engine build for Intel as well as Apple silicon; the installer is one universal download and a release checks that every slice it ships holds both architectures. - Every design token has one name: spacing, corners, fills, opacities, shadows, hit targets and glyph sizes across the Mac, iPhone and iPad views come from the shared tokens, with no visible change. Arma's themes, setup pages and identity views read the same tokens. - Upstream's update feeds moved to a new address; Arma keeps checking its own feeds in the Arma repository. - Arma's iCloud container now carries the sync record types in Production, so iCloud Sync uploads instead of reporting "Failed to send changes". - This build was made from the pre-sync commit b4e262655 with the two theme fixes and the Chromium 157.0.8103.81 universal engine (chromium-engine-934827a81220c6c0). main at this tag already carries upstream's Chromium 158.0.8127.37 engine inputs (#1322, #1323) for the next engine build.

Arma preview. Synced with upstream b69b647fc (#1309).
### Internal - Upstream's product site, its page generators, the credits list and the App Store listing moved to the upstream project; the `Website/` folder, the Pages deploy and the credits and release-page scripts are gone from the repository. The README's images now live in `Documentation/Images`. Arma's context docs drop the Website folder and point the Help Center build at `HelpCenter/build/`. - The new site-refresh workflow runs only in upstream's own repository, so it is inert on Arma.

Arma preview. Synced with upstream 4167974c2 (#1307).
### Internal - The release-notes site now builds from one exported release history: `Scripts/export-release-history.py` reads the tags, version history and note files once and writes a JSON file, and `build-release-pages.py` only renders it. Arma's per-entry note files export through it unchanged.

Arma preview. Upstream's roadmap moves with it to a new home; Arma's own links stay.
### Internal - Upstream's roadmap board now lives at the upstream project and its Xcode Cloud builds accept only the new address. Arma's About page, README and update feeds keep pointing at Arma's own repository and issues. - The macOS 15 glass stand-in and the crest-browser documentation fixes from 0.10.214 are folded into their commits.

Arma preview. The classic colours everywhere, design-system fields and buttons, and upstream's move to a new home.
### Improved - Status colours come from the classic tokens: iCloud sync and the archive list read in accent blue, green, amber and red; saved passwords and Space choices in Settings show each Space in its own accent colour, and the downloads badge takes it too. - Search rows, glyph buttons, cards and form rows across Mac, iPhone and iPad stand on the design system's components, with hover, pressed and focus states; the password save prompt's fields sit on the same field surface. - Sidebar preview cards, the lists fan and controls that appear in place grow from 80% of their size as they fade in, instead of out of a point. - The command palette's pinned, saved and open tab rows wear the same filled symbols as their sidebar sections; the globe engine mark is accent blue and the Servo mark a brand gold. - Extension badges are red with slightly larger text, and pinned extension buttons share the toolbar's hover highlight. - The badge colours follow the Space's shown look, so they match a dark window's theme.
### Internal - Upstream's project home is now the upstream project; Arma's docs and sync tooling point there. Arma's own feeds, links and repository are unchanged. - The macOS 15 glass stand-in now knows the identity glass that grouped glyph buttons use, so the Mac app still builds for macOS 15.2.

Arma preview. The classic selected-tab look, device-kept choices and What's New on the web.
### New - Settings › Appearance › More Customization lets you choose how the selected tab looks: translucent White with an opacity slider, or the device's Material; selected pins can carry their site's color. - What's New in Settings › About opens this release's page on GitHub, and the first window after an update opens the new release's page once.
### Improved - Your page zoom, background tab activity, 120 FPS, iCloud sync and per-Space download choices now live in the device store, so they survive updates and follow the same rules everywhere. - A page in a language written in another script, such as Traditional Chinese for a reader of Simplified Chinese, is offered translation; a name ending in .test counts as local and opens over HTTP first. - Every long press waits the system's half second before its menu, and lists of Spaces indent a Sub-Space past its Space's icon. - iPhone and iPad confirm a finished download and offer Reload Peek, as the Mac does. - Arma's Settings keep the Mac's own window background in light and dark, while upstream's rework names every rule once underneath.

Arma preview. Upstream spells each rule, limit and key once.
### Improved - Arma follows upstream's rework that names every limit, wait, key and web scheme in one place, so the same rules apply the same way everywhere, with the same features and no change to what you see.

Arma preview. Chromium 157.0.8103.81, and upstream's clean-up of code nothing used.
### Fixed - Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.81 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.
### Improved - Arma follows upstream's removal of code, tests and resources nothing used, with the same features in a lighter app.

Arma preview. Arma's own welcome and installer, the classic palettes as themes, a color for the palette's selected row, and the system background back under Settings.
### New - The classic twelve color palettes, Blossom, Lagoon, Lilac, Linen, Sunset, Ocean, Orchid, Citrus, Midnight, Forest, Ember and Plum, are themes beside Classic: a Space picks one from the Theme row in setup and on its page, where the swatch grid used to be. A theme's own page keeps the palettes for recoloring it. - A theme sets the color of the command palette's selected row text, light and dark, in Settings › Themes and with `arma theme` (`--palette-light-selected-text`, `--palette-dark-selected-text`). Without one the row keeps its paper's ink.
### Improved - Setup opens on Arma's banner, large, with its name lettered in blackletter and a line on who it is for, on the room's own wash; the steps follow on paper. - The installer window wears Arma's ink: the banner above the app, Arma's name lettered in blackletter, and a gold arrow to Applications. - Settings, setup, Getting Started, the command palette and the error screens sit on the window's own background again instead of the classic cream paper, so Arma matches the Mac around it. - The Start Page's title is set in Times New Roman, as the line under Arma's name on setup's welcome is.
### Fixed - Under a theme that colors the command palette's text, the selected row's text no longer takes that color on its paper and stays readable.

Arma preview. The classic chrome moves onto paper with its new Allo typeface, six audit fixes, and a WebKit crash fix.
### Improved - Headings, buttons and labels across setup, Settings, the Start Page and Getting Started use Allo, upstream's new rounded typeface; empty lists and pages, the page error title, a locked Space's name and the Settings sidebar heading use its rounded display type. - Site Controls, color pickers, permission and password prompts, hover previews and notices sit on paper in light mode instead of always being dark, and on a warm charcoal in dark mode. A Space's theme still tints them. - The command palette and the recent tabs panel sit on the same material as the address field and pinned tabs; the selected tab, the selected pin and the palette's selected row look like a sheet of light paper on every Space. - The sidebar's scroll button, widget cards, sound and sharing badges on tabs, the palette's search engine chips, the element picker, the History, Downloads and Archive buttons and the Space buttons in Settings use upstream's own surfaces and buttons instead of glass. - The page area, the error screen, the locked Space screen and empty Peek and Quick Window pages use the classic warm canvas; password prompts, the error screen and the locked Space screen use accent blue buttons on every Space. - Importing another browser's passwords brings those for sites without HTTPS too, and setup says Arma won't fill them in.
### Fixed - Fixed a crash when a page using the WebKit engine closed while it was loading another site. - Scrolling down a sidebar with long open folders no longer jumps back up, and folders inside them no longer shrink to their title and grow again as they scroll into view. - A selected tab you pick up and drag keeps its light paper look instead of turning glassy. - Making a Split View from a single tab now asks you to select at least 2 tabs, instead of asking for fewer. - When Arma can't save your session, Sync settings says why in plain words instead of showing an internal code. - A folder or Space without a name is called Untitled Folder or Untitled Space wherever it comes from, including storage and sync.

Arma preview. Smoother setup, quicker animations, adjustable Peek.
### Improved - Setup slides to its steps and hands over to Arma quickly and smoothly, without the stutter at the start or the end. - Arma's animations are quicker throughout, and switching Spaces is a little faster. - Peek opens much faster, and Peek animation time in Settings › Links sets how quickly it grows out of a link. - The command palette highlights the selected row the way the sidebar highlights the selected tab. Turn on Space accent in command palette in Appearance to tint it with the Space's accent instead.
### Fixed - Icons in the Settings sidebar turn white on the selected row, so they stay readable in light mode.

Arma preview. Settings › Themes fits the window again.
### Fixed - Settings › Themes fits the window at its usual width: where the page is narrow, the theme's preview stands above its colors instead of running past the edge.

Arma preview. Setup opens on a full welcome with its steps as chips and ends with Make It Home; crests gain a Simple set; the classic look ships as the Classic theme.
### New - Classic, the classic look of ink washing down into sky, is a theme beside Arc Sky and the Catppuccin flavors in setup and Settings › Themes. - Crests gain a Simple set, Crest, Moon, Summit, Lens, Spark and Grove, beside the Heraldic houses: a bold rounded figure raised off a soft shape.
### Improved - Setup opens on a full welcome with the steps as colored chips, each opening its step, then lays the steps beside Arma's live preview, and ends with Make It Home: the default browser, search and ad blocking. - Spaces brought in from another browser keep their own icon on a round crest in their color. - The Space picker draws a well with a neutral selector, a lighter mark for Sub-Spaces, and corners that follow the Corner radius setting; Settings shows solid glyphs in the brand colors; search engine icons in pickers are sized to their name.
### Fixed - Finishing setup no longer stalls: Arma comes up behind setup, which fades once Getting Started has drawn, and a window opening on one of Arma's own pages shows it without waiting for the content-blocking rules.

Arma preview. Setup starts every Space with a Favorites folder, and the command palette keeps typed #sections, searches words first and shows site icons on history.
### Improved - Every Space setup sets up starts with an empty Favorites folder, shown in the live preview and kept when you start browsing; file tabs into it, rename it or delete it there or later. - Return in the command palette now searches anything that isn't an address, such as a single word, with matching tabs, sites and history still listed below. An address such as github.com or localhost:3000 still opens, and the field completes one as you type it. - History results in the command palette show their site's icon with a small clock badge, so results from different sites are easy to tell apart. - Starting a crest from the Arma arms in the Crest Studio paints them in the Space's own colors, as every other house does: a red bird on a navy guidon with a gold pale and laurel on Arma's colors.
### Fixed - An address you type or paste in the command palette opens at the #section you gave it, even on a page you've visited before, and changing only the #section of the page you're on moves within that page. - A Space added in setup after you chose a theme now wears that theme in the preview too, instead of its accent's own colors.

Arma preview. Setup is a walkthrough beside a live preview, and Spaces wear a Background and an Accent.
### New - Setting up Arma is now a short walkthrough beside a live preview of the window you're building: bring tabs from another browser, choose your first Space's name, colors and icon, then add more Spaces. Close, move or file tabs in the preview and those changes carry into Arma when you start browsing. - A Space's look is now a Background and an Accent, each one color or a gradient of up to three, chosen on a color wheel with brightness and texture or taken from a palette. Crests and sidebar patterns sit under More Customization. - Setup lists each Space with its Sub-Spaces and lets you add a Sub-Space to any Space before you start browsing.
### Improved - Setup offers every theme Arma ships over each Space's colors, beside the live preview; the theme you choose dresses every Space setup makes and new Spaces after it. - Search provider chips in the command palette show their text in white or black, whichever reads better on the chip's color. - Dragging a Space's colors stays smooth while the window redraws to show them, in setup and in Settings.
### Fixed - A new Space made while a theme with a picture, such as JellyFish, is the default for new Spaces now gets the picture behind its tabs, not only the theme's colors. - Saved, pinned, reopened and imported tabs whose address holds characters such as { or [ return to the exact page they were saved at, instead of a broken search, and no longer show as moved away from their saved address.

Arma preview. Setup starts from Arma's themes and shows your crest as you shape it.
### Improved - Setup's Pick your look page now offers every theme Arma ships under Arma Themes, with the classic Heraldic, Modern and Simple looks under Classic Themes. Every card fits on one screen. - Make it yours shows a heraldic Space's crest large, on the sidebar the Space will wear, and again at the sidebar's sizes. Its sheet runs through the Crest Studio's steps: Start from, Colors, Shape, Field, Band, Emblem, Border and Finish. A chosen theme keeps the sidebar, so Start from and Shuffle change the crest alone. - Every new Space, and every preview in setup, starts with Arma's own crest. - Arma's skills for coding agents now live in .agents/skills, where Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, OpenCode and Amp find them in a checkout, with links for Claude Code and Kiro.

Arma preview. Brings in upstream's latest: folders, Clear, local network and HTTP fixes, and a smoother Chromium engine.
### New - Collapse All Folders closes every open folder in a Space at once, nested folders included, without closing any tabs. Find it in the Space's menu, in the sidebar's menu and the View menu, and in the command palette.
### Improved - Clear now keeps the tab you're on and archives your other open tabs. Hold Option to turn it into Clear All. Clear All Tabs, Option-Shift-Command-K, is also in the Tabs menu, the command palette and the Space's ••• menu. - Large folders open about twice as fast, with the folders inside them filling in just after, and a folder's preview appears without a pause even when it holds hundreds of tabs. - Folders brought in from another browser now arrive closed, nested ones included, so a large import opens to a tidy sidebar. Folders from a backup keep how you left them. - With the address bar in the sidebar, pages in Split View no longer each carry their own bar along the top: the sidebar's serves the page you're on. With the address bar on top, each page keeps its own. - Settings › Tabs now lets you choose separately what pinned tabs and saved tabs do after you close them. Your current choice carries over to both.
### Fixed - Pages in Chromium Spaces no longer flash blank or white while the next page loads after you follow a link: the page you're on stays until the next one draws. - Arma no longer quits when you clear or close the last open pages of a Chromium Space with Chromium's Contextual Tasks flag turned on. - Folder icons wider than a folder, such as a computer or a group of people, now show whole in the sidebar instead of cut off at their edge. - Chromium Spaces can open devices on your local network, such as routers, NAS drives and home servers, once you turn on Arma Helper under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network, now Arma's own setting rather than one shared with other apps. A page that can't reach a local address says how to allow it. - In Chromium Spaces, an http:// address you type or open now stays on HTTP, including when you reload it. Links on pages still try HTTPS first and fall back to HTTP when a site doesn't offer it. - Files downloaded over plain HTTP in Chromium Spaces are no longer blocked outright: Arma asks whether to keep them. - When you type a site without http:// or https://, Arma tries HTTPS first and opens it over HTTP if HTTPS can't reach it. Local addresses open over HTTP right away, and an address you type with https:// never falls back.

Arma preview. One fix for the sidebar.
### Fixed - On Mac, a folder's icon in the sidebar is no longer cut off along its left edge.

Arma preview. One fix for the terminal.
### Fixed - `arma tab unpin`, `save` and `move`, and `arma folder add`, work on a tab in any Space, not only the Space the window shows.

Arma preview. Brings in upstream 0.10, and every Arma feature rebuilt on top of Paul's code.
### New - Upstream 0.10: three styles set how much Arma shows, the address bar can sit above the page, and the sidebar gains spacing, tab size, hover previews and groups. - Settings › Appearance has a Default theme for new Spaces, or None for the classic look. Spaces you never gave a theme keep their look. - Choose how long a generated password is and which kinds of character it uses, in the strong password prompt and in Settings. - A saved password can also fill the subdomains of its site when you choose Include subdomains while saving or editing it. - Pause Arma's password prompts on a tab, for a while or until you resume them, so another password manager can fill it. - The Save password? prompt has a close button and closes on its own after the number of seconds you choose in each Space's Passwords settings. - A Space can let private windows suggest its saved passwords; a private window still never saves one.
### Improved - Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.80, with 83 upstream security fixes, five of them critical. - Showing or copying a saved password asks you to authenticate each time again by default; choose Ask Every 15 Minutes or Don't Ask in each Space's Passwords settings. - New installs follow the system's Light or Dark appearance again. - A Space's Appearance page edits its colors, sidebar and crest again under the theme it wears, with Reset Appearance back in its menu. - A closed folder shows only its loaded tabs, and a folder's header can close or unload everything in it. - The recent tabs switcher also lists the loaded tabs of the other Spaces in a Sub-Space group. - Closing a Peek shrinks it back into the link it grew out of, and a quick swipe between Spaces finishes as fast as the keyboard shortcut.
### Fixed - Settings and Getting Started show at once when Arma opens on them, instead of an empty page until you switch tabs. - The command palette no longer hangs Arma at launch or quit in a themed Space. - When the palette can't rank what you typed, Return, Tab and clicks act on the rows shown instead of waiting. - The password bubble appears only when you have a password for the site or are signing up, and closes once you move on. - With the address bar on top, clicking in the address field places the cursor and dragging selects text, instead of moving the window. - In the sidebar, a folder's icon, title and … button line up with the tabs beside it. - Choosing Modern or Simple during setup restyles your Spaces as choosing it in Settings does.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - Settings › Tabs › Open new tabs at chooses whether new tabs open at the top or the bottom of your open tabs, and can file them into the folder or Group you're in. - Back on the first page of a tab another tab opened closes it and returns to the tab that opened it. Open Link in New Tab now leads a link's menu. - Moving the pointer off the window's sidebar edge opens the hidden sidebar at once. - Notices fit their words at the top right of the page, and notices, previews and the element picker draw on one readable surface. - Pages run faster with ad blocking on, on both engines. - Arma keeps running when the disk is nearly full and a site saves data. - Save Tab and Unsave Tab in tab menus, Recent Tabs lists only loaded tabs, and Split View keeps focus on the right card under the floating sidebar and Peek. - Sparkle 2.9.6, with two installer security fixes, plus several smaller fixes.

Arma preview.
### Fixed - Split View's Arrange menu shows a drawing of each layout beside its name.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - The address bar can sit on top of the page: Settings › Appearance › Address bar › Top. Sidebar stays the default. - Each page in Split View carries its own bar with back, forward, its address, Site Controls and pinned extensions, side by side or stacked. - Pinned extensions keep the order you drag them into, in every Space that uses the profile. - Command-E opens extension popups one at a time. Archive Tab moves to Shift-Command-E. - With several sidebar tabs selected, Command-W closes them all and Command-D duplicates them again. - An import that can't be prepared shows an error instead of quitting, and Arc imports keep the names you gave tabs. - A folder's "…" button no longer covers the end of its name.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - Groups: single-level folders of open tabs at the top of a Space. Add a tab from its menu, move a selection into one, and turn a folder of open tabs into a Group or back. - Folder and Group headers have a "…" button for their menu, with Archive Tabs and Convert to Group. - A folder of open tabs, or a Group, goes away once its last tab leaves. Saved folders stay. - A new tab opens at the end of the Group or folder of the tab you are on. - Remove from Folder and Remove from Group leave the tab just below its folder or Group. - A tab filed into a folder that another device deletes moves to the top level instead of being lost.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - A narrow sidebar keeps back, forward and reload, drawn smaller where the full strip does not fit. - Going back in a tab reopened after a relaunch shows the earlier page again, on sites such as Reddit. - Revealing the hidden sidebar no longer pops up the preview of the row under the pointer, and a preview card goes when the sidebar hides. - The hidden sidebar comes out when the pointer overshoots the window's edge.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - Tab size is a slider with nine steps from 60% to 140%: Thin, Compact, Default, Comfortable and Large. Text and icons follow it half as far. - Settings › Appearance › Spacing sets the room the sidebar keeps between rows and pins and around the address field: None, Tight, Default or Relaxed. - The sidebar slides faster by default. A slide time you chose keeps its speed.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - A click anywhere on a Quick Window's address field opens it, lock included. - A Quick Window's back and forward buttons stay visible on any Space's colors. - Settings › Tabs › Keep saved tabs after unloading: turn it off and an unloaded saved tab shows an X that deletes it. Reopen Closed Tab brings it back.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - A click anywhere on the sidebar's address field opens it, not only on its line of text. - Settings › Appearance sets how long the pointer waits at the window edge before the hidden sidebar shows, from instant to 1,000 ms. - A second slider sets how fast the sidebar slides, from a snap to 480 ms.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - A folder's hover card keeps its text readable whatever Material color is set to.

Arma preview.
### From upstream - Rest the pointer on a tab or pin to see a card beside the sidebar with its title, site and the last picture of its page, without loading the page. - Rest on a folder to see all its tabs, sub-folders included, with a search; open or unload them from the card. - Settings › Appearance › Preview hover turns the cards off on this device.

Arma preview.

### From upstream 0.9.1 - A signed Arma build now proves it can load a page before it ships: packaging refuses engine helpers of an unknown kind or with the wrong entitlements, and runs the signed package's own helpers to require a page's JavaScript to run.

Arma preview.
### Arma 0.9 - Arma moves to the 0.9 line with upstream 0.9, which brings together Sub-Spaces, built-in ad blocking on Mac, iPhone and iPad, a Chromium engine built from Chromium itself at 157, and the Quick Window, Peek and appearance work. Arma's 0.8 releases already carried all of it; this build changes the version line and nothing else.

Arma preview. Chromium 157, and themes that keep their dark look.
### New - Settings › Themes has an Appearance preview that draws the windows light or dark while the page is open, so a dark look can be made and checked on a light Mac, and the other way round.
### Improved - Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.39 with upstream security and compatibility fixes. - Turning a theme's Dark look off keeps that look, so turning it back on brings your work back instead of starting over. - A theme file keeps its dark look while the look is off, so an exported theme carries both looks. - The Themes preview draws a look in the window appearance it is worn in, so Light and Dark show the difference. - `arma theme edit --unpair-dark` keeps the theme's dark look turned off, and `--dark` turns it back on.
### Fixed - A Space keeps the same colors in light and dark windows; a light look no longer goes grey when the window is dark. - A page in Chromium that asks for protected video, such as a streaming service's player, now switches to WebKit to play it with FairPlay instead of failing in Chromium.

Arma preview. Arma for Mac now needs macOS 15.2 instead of macOS 26.1.
### New - Arma for Mac runs on macOS 15.2 and later. This is the first build for macOS 15 and it has not been tried on a Mac running macOS 15 yet, so please report anything that looks or works wrong there. - On macOS 15, glass surfaces such as notices, the command palette and the element picker are drawn with a system material, and a page is translated when you ask rather than on its own.
Nothing changes on macOS 26 and later.

Arma preview. Brings in upstream's ad blocking.
### New - Arma blocks ads and trackers on every page, in WebKit and Chromium tabs, with EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock Origin's lists and a list for your language. The lists stay up to date on their own, and blocked ads leave no empty boxes. - Ad blocking has its own page in Settings and applies to every Space alike. Choose Off, Balanced or Strict, which also hides cookie notices and other annoyances. Turn single lists on or off, update them all at once, subscribe to more lists by address, and write your own rules in My Filters. - Block Element, in a page's actions, the Page menu or a right-click, hides something the lists miss. Show Blocked Elements brings it back. - Turn Off Blocking on a site from the page's actions when the site doesn't work with it. The site stays unblocked in every Space until you turn blocking on again.
### Improved - On Chromium pages, sites can no longer see which blocking rules they match or bring back what Arma hides.
### Fixed - Closing a tab while its Chromium page is full screen no longer makes Arma quit. - A full-screen Chromium page stays full screen when it moves to its next slide or video. - Settings stays smooth with hundreds of saved websites, passwords and site permissions. - Clicking the search field above saved passwords or website data lets you type in it.

Arma preview.
### Terminal - `arma tab open` places a new tab as it opens: `--pinned` or `--saved`, `--folder <path>`, and `--title` for a name of your own. - Tab and folder actions take a place in the list: `--before <row>`, `--after <row>` or `--at <n>`, where a row is a tab or a folder. `arma tab move`, `pin`, `save` and `unpin`, and `arma folder create` and `add` all take one. - `arma folder move` moves a folder, with everything in it, into another folder, to the top level, or between the saved and open tabs. - `arma theme` has one form. `arma theme edit --space <name>` changes the theme a Space uses, `arma theme use` gives it another, and `arma theme reset` puts a theme's background, icon, folders or command palette back to the plain look. The old `arma theme --space <name> [flags]` form is gone.
### Fixed - A tab filed into an empty folder joins the folder where it is, instead of carrying the folder to the end of its section. This also covers dropping a tab into an empty folder in the sidebar.

Arma preview.
